note_on_method: Every court count below is the City of Bellevue's own, from the one page where it lists them all. Every address is from that venue's own City page, which the pickleball page links to by name. Where the two pages say different things, both are quoted rather than reconciled silently. Nobody working on this has played on these courts.

slots.description: One court, and the City is precise about what kind: "1 court (over tennis net)". Cherry Crest Mini Park is a five-acre neighbourhood park in north-east Bellevue with a basketball court, picnic areas, a playground and a single tennis court with pickleball lines on it. The park's own page describes the same arrangement as "a tennis court with a pickleball overlay". There is one court here, not one of each, so a doubles game and a tennis match cannot both happen.
slots.getting_there: 2532 127th Ave NE, Bellevue, WA 98005. The City publishes nothing about parking here. This is a residential street park, not a facility with a lot, and the amenity list on its page does not include parking. Treat it as street parking of unknown availability.
slots.what_to_expect: You play over the tennis net, at a tennis net's height. Whether the court is free depends on who arrived first; the City publishes no schedule, rotation rule or booking system for any outdoor court in Bellevue. Lighting is not stated, so plan around daylight. No restroom is listed on the park's page. Around the court the page lists a playground, a tot lot for two- to five-year-olds, picnic tables and an interpretive exhibit. It is fine for a casual hit with one other pair, not somewhere to bring a group of eight.

faqs.q: Is there a net?
faqs.a: Yes, a tennis net. The City marks this venue "over tennis net" rather than "portable nets", so you play over the tennis net at its tennis height, not a pickleball net someone has set up.

faqs.q: Can I play if someone is playing tennis?
faqs.a: Not on this court. There is one court and it is the tennis court.

faqs.q: Are there restrooms or lights?
faqs.a: Neither is stated. The park page lists neither restrooms nor lighting among its amenities. Unlisted is not the same as absent; it means the City has not said.

slots.description: Four courts with portable nets on the shared tennis courts of a 34-acre park, one of the busiest public spaces in Bellevue. The City describes it as sitting "in one of the most culturally diverse neighborhoods in Bellevue", where "you will likely hear dozens of languages being spoken, but the common language is play". The park holds a water spray playground, a par-3 golf course with foot golf, the Bellevue Youth Theatre, community gardens and a skate bowl. It is also home to Crossroads Community Center, which has three indoor pickleball courts of its own, published separately because the City gives the centre its own street address.
slots.getting_there: 999 164th Ave NE, Bellevue, WA 98008. The park page lists parking among its amenities, which tells you a car park exists and nothing about whether it is full on a Saturday. The community centre in the same park has a different published address, 16000 NE 10th St, so if you are meeting someone, agree which of the two you mean.
slots.what_to_expect: Portable nets on shared tennis courts, under the City's stated default: "Bellevue's pickleball courts are shared use with tennis courts, unless otherwise noted." Four courts is the joint-largest outdoor count in the city, so this is one of the few Bellevue venues where a group can rotate. Restrooms are listed. Lighting is not stated. If the outdoor courts are taken, the indoor drop-in at the community centre in the same park is the obvious fallback. The wider park also lists an AED, electric vehicle charging, community P-patch gardens, picnic shelters and public Wi-Fi.

faqs.q: Why is it called Crossroads Park here and Crossroads Community Park on the City's list?
faqs.a: The City uses both names. Its pickleball page says "Crossroads Community Park"; the park's own page is headed "Crossroads Park" and gives that name in its contact block. The name from the park's own record is published here.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Probably. "Portable nets" describes the nets, not who supplies them, and the City does not say. The only Bellevue venue that states it provides nets is South Bellevue Community Center.

slots.description: The only venue in Bellevue where every court is pickleball and nothing else, since 1 September 2026. On 28 August the City announced that "responding to increasing community demand" it would convert the two dual-use outdoor sport courts at Eastgate Park into "a dedicated pickleball-only facility": tennis nets removed, and the four pickleball courts marked on those two courts made permanent. The park's own page lists "four dedicated pickleball courts" alongside a ballfield, picnic tables, a play area and nature trails. A follow-up project is planned to resurface the courts "with only pickleball lines, creating durable and consistent play conditions".
slots.getting_there: 14500 SE Newport Way, Bellevue, WA 98006, in the Eastgate neighbourhood in the south-east of the city. Nine street numbers along the same road, at 14509 SE Newport Way, is South Bellevue Community Center and its six indoor courts. The City publishes nothing about parking at the park.
slots.what_to_expect: Four dedicated courts, no booking, and no published hours beyond the City's own phrasing: the courts "will remain first-come, first-serve and will be open during posted park hours". Two questions are open. The City does not say what, if anything, replaced the tennis nets it removed, so bring a net if you have one. And the resurfacing is announced rather than done, so the lines may still be the old dual-use markings. Lighting is not stated. The tennis players who used these courts have been directed to Silver Leaf, Lakemont, Spiritridge and Sunset, "all within approximately three miles of Eastgate Park"; Lakemont and Spiritridge are pickleball venues too.

faqs.q: Are these really pickleball-only courts?
faqs.a: Yes, as of 1 September 2026. The City removed the tennis nets from two dual-use sport courts and said the transition to pickleball-only use is permanent. Its pickleball page marks the venue "4 courts (dedicated)".

faqs.q: Will more Bellevue courts be converted?
faqs.a: Not according to the City. The same notice says the department "does not currently have conversions planned at any other dual-use courts in Bellevue".

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: The City's park page lists a ballfield, picnic tables, a play area and nature trails. It does not list restrooms or parking, which means the City has not said, not that there are none.

slots.description: One of only nine venues in this entire directory with a court count above zero on both sides, and the first: three indoor and two outdoor, at one address. The City lists them as two entries on its pickleball page, "Hidden Valley Fieldhouse: 3 courts" under Indoor and "Hidden Valley Sports Park: 2 courts (portable nets)" under Outdoor, and links both names to the same park page, so they are published here as one place. The park is 17.31 acres with three softball fields, a lighted tennis court, a sports court and restrooms at both the north and south ends.
slots.getting_there: 1903 112th Ave NE, Bellevue, WA 98004, in the north-west of the city near the Bellevue-Kirkland line. The park page lists parking among its amenities. The fieldhouse is a building inside the park, so one address gets you both the indoor courts and the outdoor ones.
slots.what_to_expect: Two outdoor courts with portable nets on shared tennis courts, and three indoor courts in the fieldhouse on whatever schedule the fieldhouse is running. The City publishes no price for the indoor courts, pointing instead at its registration site and at drop-in schedule PDFs dated 2023 and 2024. The park page mentions "a lighted tennis court", singular, alongside a separate sports court, and nothing says the pickleball is played on the lit one, so lighting stays unstated. The page also lists a basketball court, an exercise area and gym, public Wi-Fi and "restrooms at the north and south end of the park".

faqs.q: How many courts are there in total?
faqs.a: Five: three indoor in the fieldhouse and two outdoor in the park. That makes it one of only nine venues anywhere in this directory offering both, which is a statement about what we have covered, not a claim about the rest of America.

faqs.q: Are the outdoor courts lit?
faqs.a: Not stated. The park has "a lighted tennis court" according to its own page, but it also has a separate sports court, and the City never says which surface the two pickleball courts are on.

faqs.q: What does the indoor session cost?
faqs.a: The City does not publish a price for the fieldhouse. It says "Pickleball schedules and fees can be viewed on our registration site, or on a community center's drop-in schedule", so a fee may apply.

slots.description: Three courts on a 4.2-acre park just south of Crossroads, and the only venue in Bellevue where the City splits its own count: "3 courts (1 dedicated, 2 portable nets)". One court is pickleball and nothing else; two are portable nets on the park's two tennis courts. The park page words it as "three pickleball courts (one dedicated, two overlay)", alongside paved trails, a basketball court, a play area, a picnic area and seasonal restrooms.
slots.getting_there: 15803 NE 6th St, Bellevue, WA 98008, a few blocks south of Crossroads Park and its four outdoor courts, which makes this corner of Bellevue the densest cluster of courts in the city. The park's amenity list does not include parking, and the City publishes nothing about where to leave a car.
slots.what_to_expect: One dedicated court you can rely on and two that depend on whether anyone wants to play tennis. Restrooms are on the park page and described as seasonal, so do not count on them in February. No outdoor court in Bellevue can be reserved and the City publishes no rotation rule. Lighting is not stated. If the dedicated court is taken, Crossroads Park a few blocks north is the shortest walk to an alternative anywhere in Bellevue. The imported row this directory started from said one court here; the City says three, and the City owns the park.

faqs.q: Are the restrooms open all year?
faqs.a: The park page calls them "seasonal restrooms", which is the City's word. It does not publish the season.

faqs.q: Is the dedicated court bookable?
faqs.a: No. No outdoor pickleball court anywhere in Bellevue can be reserved. It is first come, and after that it is whatever the people on court are doing.

faqs.q: What else is in the park?
faqs.a: Paved trails, two tennis courts, a basketball court, a play area, a tot lot, a picnic area and seasonal restrooms, on 4.2 acres.

slots.description: Four courts overlaid on two tennis courts, in a 16-acre park in the Lakemont neighbourhood in Bellevue's south-east corner. The park page does the arithmetic for you: "four pickleball courts (overlay on the two tennis courts)". Around the courts are a play area, two picnic shelters, a basketball court, a skate bowl, restrooms, a softball field, and more than three miles of trails that connect through to Lewis Creek Park, whose two courts are the next nearest in this directory.
slots.getting_there: 5170 Village Park Drive SE, Bellevue, WA 98006. Parking is listed among the park's amenities. The park sits above the Lewis Creek valley, and the City warns that portions of the trail down are steep or use stairs, which matters if you were thinking of walking between the two venues rather than driving.
slots.what_to_expect: Four courts sharing two tennis courts with portable nets, under the City's default of shared use unless marked otherwise. Lakemont is one of the four parks the City pointed tennis players toward when it converted Eastgate to pickleball-only, so demand on those tennis courts may not be going down. Restrooms are listed. Lighting is not stated. This is the largest outdoor count in south-east Bellevue and the natural first stop on that side of I-90. The two picnic shelters near the skate park can each be rented for up to 25 guests.

faqs.q: How can there be four courts on two courts?
faqs.a: Because pickleball courts are smaller. The park page states "four pickleball courts (overlay on the two tennis courts)", so the four is a count of pickleball courts marked out, not of separate court structures.

faqs.q: Can I book a shelter for a group?
faqs.a: Yes, though not a court. The City rents two picnic shelters here, each for up to 25 guests, through its park rental page. The pickleball courts cannot be reserved.

slots.description: Two courts, and the only ones in Bellevue that are not sharing with tennis: the City lists them as "2 courts (basketball court overlay, portable nets)". That single parenthesis is the most specific thing any operator in this directory has said about what a pickleball court is drawn on top of. Lewis Creek Park is the most facility-like of Bellevue's park sites, with a ranger station and visitor centre, interpretive exhibits, ranger-led events, hiking trails through the creek valley, a baseball field and restrooms. The pickleball is a small part of a park people visit for other reasons.
slots.getting_there: 5808 Lakemont Blvd SE, Bellevue, WA 98006, below and west of Lakemont Community Park, to which it is connected by trail. Parking is listed among the amenities, and this is one of the few Bellevue park pages that also lists an information kiosk and a visitor centre, so the site is set up for people arriving who have not been before.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts marked on a basketball court, with portable nets. The surface is a basketball surface, the lines are shared with basketball lines, and whether the court is free depends on a different sport than at every other Bellevue venue. The park's own page does not mention pickleball at all; the count comes from the City's pickleball page. Restrooms are listed. Lighting is not stated. Come for the park and treat the pickleball as a bonus rather than a plan.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Assume so. "Portable nets" tells you the nets are portable and not who brings them, and a basketball court has no net at the right height to borrow.

faqs.q: Is this a good park to bring people who do not play?
faqs.a: Probably the best in Bellevue for that. The City lists a ranger station and visitor centre, ranger-led events, wildlife viewing, a scenic viewpoint, interpretive exhibits and trails through the Lewis Creek valley, with restrooms and parking on site.

slots.description: Two courts played over the tennis nets on a 1.65-acre neighbourhood park, the smallest park in Bellevue's set, and one of only two venues in the city where the City marks the courts "over tennis net" rather than giving them portable nets. The park page describes "2 tennis courts with pickleball overlay, playground, picnic area, and a basketball/multi-purpose sport court". As at Cherry Crest, the tennis net's height is the net's height, and a tennis match is a pickleball closure.
slots.getting_there: 12309 SE 23rd Place, Bellevue, WA 98005, in the Norwood Village neighbourhood south of I-90 and west of Eastgate. Parking is not among the amenities on the park's page and the City publishes nothing about it. This is a residential pocket park, so plan on the street.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts, no nets to set up, no booking, and no lighting stated. On a park of under two acres there is nowhere to wait but the side of the court, so this is a venue for a pair or two rather than a group. The City names it "Norwood Village Park" on its pickleball list and "Norwood Village Neighborhood Park" on the park's own page; the longer name is published here because it is the one in the park's own record. No restroom is listed, which means the City has not said, not that there is none.

faqs.q: Is it worth the trip?
faqs.a: If you live nearby, yes. If you are driving across Bellevue, the four-court venues at Crossroads, Eastgate and Lakemont give a group somewhere to rotate, and this one does not.

faqs.q: Do the courts share with anything besides tennis?
faqs.a: No. The two pickleball courts are lines on the park's two tennis courts, and you play over the tennis net. The separate basketball/multi-purpose sport court carries no pickleball markings the City mentions.

slots.description: Two courts with portable nets on shared tennis courts, in the Spiritridge neighbourhood of south Bellevue. This is the thinnest record of Bellevue's venues: the City states the count on its pickleball page, the park's own page gives the address and says nothing about pickleball, and nothing else about the venue is published anywhere. What is on the record is that Spiritridge is one of the four parks the City named as a tennis alternative when it converted Eastgate Park to pickleball-only in September 2026, and its tennis courts are its pickleball courts.
slots.getting_there: 16100 SE 33rd Place, Bellevue, WA 98008. The park page lists no parking amenity and the City publishes no guidance, so treat it as a residential street park with parking of unknown availability.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts under the City's stated default: shared use with tennis, portable nets, first come. No restrooms are listed, no lighting is stated, and no surface is stated. After the Eastgate conversion the City has actively directed tennis players here, which is the most useful thing anyone can honestly say about turning up on a weekend. The count, the address, the county and the postcode all come from City pages. The park's size, its amenities and whether there is a restroom do not, because the City's page for this park says none of it.

faqs.q: Will it be busy with tennis?
faqs.a: Possibly more than it was. When the City converted Eastgate Park's dual-use courts to pickleball-only on 1 September 2026, it named Spiritridge among the nearby parks that "continue to offer public tennis courts". These are the same courts pickleball shares.

faqs.q: Do I need to bring a net?
faqs.a: Assume so. "Portable nets" describes the net, not who carries it, and nothing on either City page says the park supplies one.

faqs.q: Are there restrooms or parking?
faqs.a: Not stated. Spiritridge Park's page gives the address and little else. That is a gap in the City's record rather than a statement that the park lacks them.

slots.description: Three indoor courts in a full-service community centre inside Crossroads Park, running as drop-in sessions alongside table tennis, basketball, volleyball and, on the City's own list, indoor kite flying. The centre's programme page states the rule that matters more than any schedule: "No registration required: first-come, first-served. Space is limited." It is one of four indoor pickleball venues in Bellevue.
slots.getting_there: 16000 NE 10th St, Bellevue, WA 98008. This is inside Crossroads Park, whose own four outdoor pickleball courts are published under a different address, 999 164th Ave NE: the same park, two City addresses, two venues in this directory. If you are meeting someone for a game, say which one you mean.
slots.what_to_expect: Three courts, no booking, and a capacity you cannot see from outside: "Space is limited" is the City's phrase and it does not publish a number. It does not publish the price either. The pickleball page says "Pickleball schedules and fees can be viewed on our registration site, or on a community center's drop-in schedule", and the drop-in schedule linked for this centre is a PDF dated 2023. If cost matters, ring ahead. The pickleball shares a gym with the rest of a busy drop-in programme, so the schedule decides whether the courts exist on the day you turn up. Outdoors the courts are always there and possibly occupied; indoors they are only there during the session.

faqs.q: Do I need to register?
faqs.a: No. The centre's programme page says of its drop-in activities: "No registration required: first-come, first-served. Space is limited." There is no booking system for pickleball at any Bellevue venue.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: Not stated. The City states no price for pickleball here. The only Bellevue venue that publishes a price is South Bellevue Community Center, at $4 for residents and $5 for non-residents.

slots.description: Two indoor courts, and the only venue on Bellevue's pickleball list that comes with a warning attached to the count: "2 courts (with low ceiling)". The centre is Bellevue's hub for older adults, covering health and wellness, cultural and performing arts, human services, community dining and trips, and it also runs drop-in sports and fitness for adults 18 and up, which is where the pickleball sits. It is the smallest indoor count in the city.
slots.getting_there: 4063 148th Ave NE, Bellevue, WA 98007, in the north-east of the city. Other directories may place this centre in Redmond; the imported record this project started from did. The City's own page places it in Bellevue, and the Census geocoder matched it to Bellevue city, King County.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts, indoors, on a published drop-in schedule, in a room the City itself describes as having a low ceiling. Lobs are the obvious casualty. The City publishes no price for pickleball here and the drop-in schedule it links is a PDF dated 2024, so confirm both the timetable and the cost before you drive. If a low ceiling is a problem, South Bellevue's six courts are the alternative on the other side of the city. The City states that the centre "offers a variety of drop-in sports & fitness activities for adults 18 and up", with services for youth and adults of all ages on evenings and weekends.

faqs.q: What does "low ceiling" mean in practice?
faqs.a: The City does not say how low. It is the one venue on its list where the room, rather than the court, carries a caveat, so treat overhead shots as unreliable and expect a flatter game.

faqs.q: Is this centre only for older adults?
faqs.a: No. The City describes a comprehensive programme of senior services and also states that the centre "offers a variety of drop-in sports & fitness activities for adults 18 and up".

slots.description: Six indoor courts, the largest single count in Bellevue, and the only venue in the city that publishes what it costs to play. Adult drop-in sessions are $4 for Bellevue residents and $5 for everyone else; family sessions are free, on condition that an adult and a child under 18 from the same household are on court together. It is also the only Bellevue venue that says who supplies the equipment: "We provide pickleball balls, nets, and poles. Participants should plan to bring their own paddles, but a few extras are available to borrow if needed."
slots.getting_there: 14509 SE Newport Way, Bellevue, WA 98006, in Eastgate. Nine street numbers away, at 14500 SE Newport Way, is Eastgate Park and its four dedicated outdoor courts, the only address pair in this directory putting a city's largest indoor venue and its only pickleball-only outdoor courts on one road. The City publishes no parking guidance for either.
slots.what_to_expect: Turn up with a paddle, check in at the front desk, and pay at the door. Nothing can be held: "All Drop-In Sports times are strictly drop-in only", and "reservations, saving spots and/or signing in for another participant is not allowed". Capacity varies: "Each program has a different maximum capacity depending on the time/day and how much space there is available in the gym(s) that day." The gym is shared with badminton, basketball and volleyball drop-ins, so how many of the six courts are up depends on the session. Coaching is not permitted at drop-in sessions; clinics and classes are separate, registered and priced. The City also mentions play passes, with details at the front desk.

faqs.q: What does it cost?
faqs.a: $4 for Bellevue residents and $5 for non-residents, per adult drop-in session. Family drop-in sports are free, but a family session requires an adult and a child under 18 from the same household playing together. It is not a route for two adults.

faqs.q: Can I bring a coach?
faqs.a: Not to a drop-in session. The centre states that as a publicly owned facility it "cannot allow coaching of any kind at any of the Adult and/or Family Drop-In Sports Programs". Clinics and classes require registration.

slots.description: Four courts played with portable nets, per the City's pickleball page, in a park that also holds the Highland Community Center and the Bellevue Skate Park. This is the most lightly evidenced venue in Bellevue. The City's pickleball page lists "Highland Community Park: 4 courts (portable nets)". The park's own page, the record card the City keeps for the site, never mentions pickleball at all: it describes "a lighted baseball field, a lighted softball field, two tennis courts, a play area, and picnic tables", and lists "Tennis Courts" among the amenities. Nothing there contradicts the count, but it is stated once rather than twice.
slots.getting_there:
14224 Bel-Red Road, Bellevue, WA 98007, in the Bel-Red corridor. This address is why the venue took until 4 September 2026 to appear here: the US Census address geocoder returns no match for it, nor for four spelling variants, and a second resolver, OpenStreetMap, now resolves it at house-number level. The county and postcode published here come from OpenStreetMap rather than from the Census.

Parking and restrooms are both listed among the park's amenities, which is more than most Bellevue park pages offer, and the site is shared with a community center, so it is set up for people arriving by car.
slots.what_to_expect: Four courts, portable nets, no published cost and no published hours. Bring a net: "portable nets" says the nets are portable, not who brings them. Restrooms are listed. Lighting is not stated for the courts: the park page calls the baseball and softball fields lighted and says nothing about lighting on the tennis courts the pickleball shares. The City calls this park two different things on two of its own pages, "Highland Community Park" where it counts the courts and "Highland Park" where it describes the site. The name from the venue's own page is published here. If you are searching the City's site, try both.

faqs.q: How many courts are there?
faqs.a: Four, with portable nets. The City's pickleball page reads "Highland Community Park: 4 courts (portable nets)". That is the only City page that states a pickleball count for this site.

faqs.q: Are the courts lit?
faqs.a: Not stated. The park page describes a lighted baseball field and a lighted softball field, and says nothing about lighting on the tennis courts.
